about: ChatGPT, Claude and Microsoft Copilot as outside systems (Adam, Nov 18 2026: three boxes; a play offers them whenever a product on its canvas connects to them; lines that sell no hours are fine; no Adobe Analytics lines). The 41 connections and six services of handoff/2026-11-17/ai_hosts/proposal_data_v2.json, whose quotes were proven word for word on Adobe's pages on Nov 18 2026 (Experience League, Adobe Help, Adobe Developer, www.adobe.com, Frame.io's help site, aem.live, and the business.adobe.com post Adam pasted); the quotes are kept with each connection in connection_types.json. The lines carry no services of their own: each line's work sits on its Adobe product's service, counted once, and a line whose person adds Adobe's connector alone sells no hours. No line is typed a native integration (Adobe does not use the word for these assistants), so the lines are drawn plain. Hours are our own estimates; Adobe publishes none.

lines.name: Customer Journey Analytics questions in ChatGPT, Claude or Microsoft Copilot
lines.scope: Add the read-only or the full assistant permission to the product profiles of your client's pilot users in the Admin Console, help each person add Adobe's Customer Journey Analytics plugin in ChatGPT or connector in Claude and sign in with their Adobe ID, agree the data view each team uses, compare the first answers with Analysis Workspace, and write the starter questions and a one-page guide.
lines.evidence: Other users must be added to an Adobe Admin Console product profile that includes the MCP Read-only Access or MCP Full Access permission item.

source.title: Adobe Developer: Analytics, Frequently asked questions

lines.name: Workfront in ChatGPT, Claude or Microsoft Copilot: rollout and write access

Where a Coworker service on the same quote already set these permissions or made the write decision, this service reuses them.
lines.evidence: Your Workfront administrator controls MCP server access for your Workfront instance through two toggles in System Preferences: Read-only MCP tools (enabled by default) and Write MCP tools (disabled by default).

notes: Every service starts off (default false), like the Figma services, so a canvas saved before Nov 18 reopens with the same services and totals.

Reused, not repeated: Coworker set up in an AI platform (CW08, on Coworker), Run-Workflow MCP for AI agents (FP07, on Firefly Creative Production), Data feeds and Data Warehouse exports (AN07, on Adobe Analytics) and Paid media connections and activation setup (GS04, on GenStudio for Performance Marketing).
XT05 covers Workfront Planning too, so Planning gets no service of its own.

Overlap review: XT05 with Coworker rollout and write access (XB14) and Coworker access and tool permissions for Planning (XJ32); XT06 with Coworker prompts for GenStudio reporting and drafts (XG08). The canvas and the statement of work flag each pair when both are on.

The lines to AEM Sites and XT03 need AEM Sites as its own product: Adobe's AEM page covers AEM as a Cloud Service and does not mention Edge Delivery Services, so they do not show while AEM Sites is the AEM authoring of an Edge Delivery site, where the Edge Delivery lines (Experience Workspace, on aem.live) go to Edge Delivery Services itself.
basis and bands are each service's sizes in the build data; like the Figma services, the statement of work treats these services as service concepts whose quantity the partner writes.
